children: The U.S. deficit-to-GDP level declined to 5.7%-5.8% for the fiscal year 2026 from the “astounding level” of ~6.3% that the Trump administration inherited from the prior administration, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday.
"We would have continued that fiscal contraction this year but for the tariff refunds," he said during his testimony to the House of Representatives Financial Services Committee
"We will talk about a fiscal consolidation — that is coming," he added.
Under President Donald Trump's second term, the private sector created more than 1M jobs, and real wages are outpacing inflation, he said in his prepared opening statement. However,
increased 3.1% Y/Y in the same month, according to recent data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Bessent emphasized the administration's role in focusing international financial supervisory entities. During the G20 Finance Ministerial meetings earlier this month, economies representing more than two-thirds of global GDP agreed to address excessive and persistent imbalances, advance financial literacy, improve the global sovereign debt architecture, and support regulatory modernization.

"In substance and in spirit, these priorities reflect the administration’s approach to international institutions by ensuring that American time and resources serve American interests," Bessent said. "We are also bringing that same discipline to the IMF and World Bank so they remain true to their core mandates and are better positioned to promote economic growth."
